items.prompt: Put the life cycle of a chicken in order. Start with the egg.
hints: The chicken life cycle starts with an egg.
Ask: what hatches out of the egg?
Put the egg first, then think about what comes out of it.
items.explanation: A chick hatches from the egg. It grows into a young chicken and then an adult hen, which lays more eggs.

items.prompt: Put the life cycle of a frog in order.
hints: Start with the eggs in the pond.
Which stage has a tail and no legs?
Frogspawn comes first. What hatches from it?
items.explanation: Frogspawn hatches into tadpoles. Tadpoles grow legs and become froglets, and froglets grow into adult frogs.

items.prompt: Put the life cycle of a butterfly in order.
hints: A butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf.
Which stage eats lots of leaves?
Start with the egg. What hatches from it?
items.explanation: A caterpillar hatches from the egg and eats lots of leaves. It makes a chrysalis, and a butterfly comes out of it.

items.prompt: What hatches from a butterfly's egg?

figure.alt: A tiny butterfly egg on a leaf.

options.why: The butterfly comes later, after the chrysalis.

hints: The young butterfly does not look like its parent.
Think about the stage that eats lots of leaves.
Remember the order: egg, then what?
items.explanation: A caterpillar hatches from a butterfly's egg. Later it becomes a chrysalis and then a butterfly.

items.prompt: Which frog stage has a long tail and lives only in water?

figure.alt: Stages of a frog: frogspawn, a tadpole with a long tail, and an adult frog.

options.why: Frogspawn is the eggs. They do not have tails yet.
An adult frog has no tail and can live on land.
A froglet has legs and only a tiny tail. It can leave the water.

hints: Think about the stage that swims like a little fish.
Which stage has no legs at first?
Remember the order: frogspawn, then what hatches?
items.explanation: A tadpole has a long tail and lives only in water. It breathes through gills, like a fish, until it grows legs and lungs.

items.prompt: How does each animal have young? Sort the cards.
hints: Birds, frogs and turtles lay eggs.
Animals with fur or hair usually give birth and feed their babies milk.
Start with the whale. Does the mother feed her baby milk?
items.explanation: Hens, turtles and frogs lay eggs. Cows, cats and whales give birth to babies and feed them milk.

items.prompt: Why do we call it a life cycle?

options.why: Animals and plants both have life cycles.

options.text: The stages repeat when adults have young.
Each animal walks round in circles.
options.why: Cycle here means the stages repeat. It is not about moving in circles.

options.text: It stops after the adult stage.
options.why: Adults have young, so the cycle starts again.

hints: Think about what a frog does once it is an adult.
Where do new frogspawn eggs come from?
Draw the stages in a circle in your mind. What joins the end to the start?
items.explanation: Adults have young, and the young grow up to have young of their own. The stages repeat again and again, like a circle.

items.prompt: Match each young animal to its adult.
hints: Some young animals look like their parents and some do not.
Do the names you know first.
Start with the tadpole. What does it turn into?
items.explanation: A tadpole becomes a frog and a caterpillar becomes a butterfly. A duckling grows into a duck, a foal into a horse and a cub into a lion.

items.prompt: Put the life cycle of a plant in order.
hints: Every plant starts from something small in the soil.
The flower comes before the fruit.
Start with the seed. What grows from it first?
items.explanation: A seed grows into a seedling and then a young plant. The plant grows flowers, and the flowers turn into fruits with new seeds inside.

items.prompt: What is a seedling?

figure.alt: A seed, a seedling with a small shoot and two leaves, and a bigger plant.

options.why: A seedling has grown out of a seed. It has a shoot and roots.
Flowers come later, when the plant is older.

hints: The word seedling has seed in it. What comes just after a seed?
Ask: is it older or younger than a flowering plant?
items.explanation: A seedling is a very young plant that has just grown from a seed. It has a small shoot, roots and its first leaves.

items.prompt: Put the stages of a human life in order.
hints: Think of the people in your family from youngest to oldest.
Put the baby first, then think who comes next.
items.explanation: Humans grow from a baby to a child, a teenager, an adult and then an older adult. Adults can have babies, so the cycle goes on.

items.prompt: A whale lives in the sea like a fish. How is a baby whale born?

figure.alt: A whale swimming in the sea.

options.why: Many fish lay eggs. Whales do not, because a whale is a mammal.

options.text: Its mother gives birth to it and feeds it milk.
It starts life as a tadpole.

hints: Living in the sea does not make an animal a fish.
Whales breathe air and feed their babies milk.
Think about how a cow or a cat has its young.
items.explanation: A whale is a mammal. The mother gives birth to a live baby and feeds it milk, just like a cow or a cat.

items.prompt: Which animal's life cycle has a resting stage in a hard case?

options.why: A tadpole changes slowly while it swims. It does not rest in a case.
A chick just grows bigger. It does not rest in a case.
A kitten just grows bigger. It does not rest in a case.

hints: Think about a stage that hangs still from a leaf or a twig.
This stage is called a chrysalis.
Ask: which animal has a chrysalis in its life cycle?
items.explanation: A caterpillar makes a hard case called a chrysalis. Inside it, the caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

items.prompt: In which pair do both young look very different from their parents?

options.why: Kittens and puppies look like small adults.
Ducklings look like small ducks, and calves look like small cows.
Foals and cubs look like small adults.

hints: Think about the young of each animal.
Which young animals change shape as they grow?
Picture a tadpole and a caterpillar. What do they become?
items.explanation: A young frog is a tadpole and a young butterfly is a caterpillar. Both look very different from their parents and change a lot as they grow.

items.prompt: A hen's egg takes about 21 days to hatch. Tegar's hen starts sitting on her eggs on 1 May. On what date in May should they hatch?

figure.alt: A hen sits on her eggs for 21 days before the chicks hatch.

hints: The eggs need about 21 days of sitting.
Add 21 days to the start date.
Start at 1 May and count on 21 days.
items.explanation: 1 May plus 21 days is 22 May. The chicks should hatch around 22 May.

items.prompt: Draw the life cycle of a frog. Use arrows to show the order.

criteria.label: Draws frogspawn, a tadpole, a froglet and a frog
Puts the stages in the right order
Uses arrows in a circle to show the cycle

hints: Start with frogspawn in a pond.
Draw arrows from each stage to the next, and from the frog back to the eggs.
items.explanation: Frogspawn hatches into tadpoles, tadpoles become froglets and froglets grow into frogs. Adult frogs lay frogspawn, so the cycle starts again.

items.prompt: A tadpole grows into a ___.
hints: Tadpoles live in water and grow legs.
items.explanation: A tadpole grows into a frog. Frogs begin as eggs, then tadpoles.

items.prompt: Put the frog life cycle in the table. Fill in the missing stages.
hints: A frog starts as an egg.
The second stage lives in water and has a tail.
items.explanation: The stages are egg, tadpole and frog.
items.caption: Frog life cycle
head: Stage
Name

items.prompt: Draw the life cycle of a butterfly on paper. Draw arrows between the stages. Then take a photo.
hints: A butterfly starts as an egg.
A caterpillar hatches and eats leaves.
items.explanation: The stages are egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and butterfly. Arrows show the order.

criteria.label: Puts the stages in the right order
Uses arrows to show the order

items.prompt: Label the stages of the frog life cycle.
hints: A frog begins life as an egg.
The second stage lives in water and has a tail.
items.explanation: The stages are egg, tadpole and frog, in that order.

items.prompt: Label the stages of the butterfly life cycle. One label is not needed.
hints: A caterpillar hatches from an egg.
The chrysalis is where the caterpillar changes.
items.explanation: The stages shown are caterpillar, chrysalis and butterfly. The egg comes before them.

items.prompt: What hatches from a hen's egg?

options.why: A calf is a baby cow.
A puppy is a baby dog.
A lamb is a baby sheep.

items.explanation: A chick hatches from a hen's egg.

items.prompt: Which butterfly stage looks like a worm with legs?

options.why: An egg is small and round.
A chrysalis is a hard case.

items.explanation: A caterpillar looks like a worm with legs. It eats lots of leaves.

items.prompt: What comes out of a frog's egg?
hints: It is not a frog yet.
items.explanation: A tadpole hatches from a frog's egg. It lives in the water and has a tail.

items.prompt: What happens inside a chrysalis?

options.text: The caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

items.explanation: Inside the hard case, the caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

items.prompt: How does a baby kitten get its food at first?

options.text: It drinks milk from its mother.

items.explanation: Baby kittens drink their mother's milk.

items.prompt: Which animal does not lay eggs?
items.explanation: A rabbit gives birth to live babies. Hens, frogs and butterflies lay eggs.

items.prompt: What must a seed have to start a new plant?
items.explanation: A seed needs water and warmth to begin to grow.

items.prompt: A tadpole has grown four legs. What does it become next?

options.why: A tadpole is not a fish.

hints: It comes out of the water.
items.explanation: The tadpole loses its tail and becomes a small frog.

items.prompt: Does the young look very different from its parent? Sort the cards.
items.explanation: A caterpillar, a tadpole and a bee grub look very different from their parents. A puppy, a kitten and a baby rabbit look like their parents.

items.prompt: Choose all the animals that start life as an egg.
items.explanation: Frogs, butterflies and hens start life as eggs. Cows, dogs and monkeys give birth to live young.

items.prompt: Put the duck's life in order. Start with the egg.
items.explanation: A duck begins as an egg. It hatches into a duckling and grows into a duck.

items.prompt: Match each butterfly stage to what it is like.
items.explanation: The egg is laid on a leaf and the caterpillar eats leaves. The chrysalis is a hard case and the butterfly has wings.

items.prompt: A hen lays an ___. It hatches into a ___.
hints: A chick is a baby hen.
items.explanation: A hen lays an egg. A chick hatches from it.

items.prompt: Name the young animal.
head: Adult
Young
hints: A chick comes from an egg.
items.explanation: A young frog is a tadpole and a young butterfly is a caterpillar. A young hen is a chick and a young sheep is a lamb.

items.prompt: Zuri finds frogspawn in a pond. Some weeks later tiny tadpoles swim in the water. Then the tadpoles grow four legs. Later they leave the water as small frogs.

parts.prompt: What do the eggs turn into?
How many legs does a tadpole grow?

items.explanation: The eggs hatch into tadpoles. The tadpoles grow four legs.

items.prompt: A butterfly lays 40 eggs. Half of them hatch. How many caterpillars is that?
items.explanation: Half of 40 is 20, so 20 caterpillars hatch.

items.prompt: Tap the caterpillar.
items.explanation: The caterpillar is the long, soft stage that eats leaves.

items.prompt: Tap the stage that has wings.
items.explanation: The adult butterfly has wings.

items.prompt: Label the stages of a plant's life.

figure.alt: A seed, a seedling and a grown plant.

items.explanation: A plant begins as a seed. It grows into a small seedling and then a grown plant.

items.prompt: A baby frog with a tail lives in water. It is called a ___.
items.explanation: A baby frog with a tail is a tadpole.

items.prompt: Which order is right for a butterfly?
hints: The chrysalis is before the adult.
items.explanation: A butterfly starts as an egg. Then it is a caterpillar, a chrysalis and finally a butterfly.

items.prompt: Mina finds a small animal with six legs eating leaves. It has no wings. After some weeks it makes a hard case. What is it likely to be?
items.explanation: A caterpillar eats leaves and then makes a chrysalis.

items.prompt: A frog lays 100 eggs. Only 10 grow into adult frogs. How many do not?
items.explanation: 100 - 10 = 90. Most eggs do not become adult frogs because many are eaten.
